rate.label: CNY per USD (IRS 2025 yearly average for China)
rate.note: Used only to restate CNY-denominated published tariffs in USD. It is not a live executable rate and the IRS states it has no official exchange rate.

sources.title: 2026 personal FX FAQ (08): how does a foreign individual purchase and remit employment income earned in China?
sources.publisher: State Administration of Foreign Exchange, Tianjin branch
sources.quote: 境外个人在境内取得的经常项目合法人民币收入，凭本人有效身份证件和有交易额的购汇资金来源材料（含税务凭证）在银行办理购汇
sources.supports: Foreign individuals convert lawful current-account RMB income at a bank with valid ID plus source-of-funds materials including tax vouchers (quoting Huifa [2020] No. 14 Art. 59).

sources.title: Implementing Rules of the Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange (Huifa [2007] No. 1, amended republication)
sources.quote: 第二条对个人结汇和境内个人购汇实行年度总额管理。年度总额分别为每人每年等值5万美元。 / 第十三条（一）在境内取得的经常项目合法人民币收入，凭本人有效身份证件和有交易额的相关证明材料（含税务凭证）办理购汇。
sources.supports: The USD 50,000 annual total applies to domestic individuals' purchase/sale of FX (Art. 2); foreign individuals' lawful current-account RMB income is handled under Art. 13 with ID and transaction materials including tax vouchers. Art. 30/31 set USD 10,000 cash withdrawal and USD 5,000 cash deposit bank thresholds. Art. 39 is noted as repealed by Huifa [2023] No. 8.

sources.title: 2026 personal FX FAQ (10): may a foreign individual reconvert unused RMB, and on what documents?
sources.publisher: State Administration of Foreign Exchange, Tianjin branch
sources.quote: 原兑换水单的兑回有效期为自兑换日起24个月；对于当日累计兑换不超过等值500美元（含）以及离境前在境内关外场所当日累计不超过等值1000美元（含）的兑换，可凭本人有效身份证件办理
sources.supports: Reconversion of unused RMB requires the original exchange memo within 24 months; ID-only same-day amounts up to USD 500 (USD 1,000 in restricted areas before departure).

sources.title: 2024 current-account FX policy Q&A case (9): do foreign individuals enjoy the annual facilitation quota?
sources.publisher: State Administration of Foreign Exchange, Tianjin branch
sources.quote: 持有外国人永久居留身份证的境外个人适用购汇年度便利化额度。
sources.supports: Only foreign individuals holding a PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card get the annual facilitation quota for FX purchase; others use the documented-income route.

sources.title: Circular on Regulating Large-sum Overseas Cash Withdrawals with Bank Cards (Huifa [2017] No. 29)
sources.quote: the sum of withdrawals using the bank cards under the name of the individual (including supplementary cards) shall not exceed the equivalent of RMB 100,000 in every civil year ... the ceiling for every foreign currency card per day is to be adjusted from the equivalent of USD 1,000 to the equivalent of RMB 10,000
sources.supports: Overseas ATM withdrawals with mainland-issued cards are capped at RMB 100,000 per person per calendar year and RMB 10,000 per card per day; exceeding the annual cap suspends overseas cash withdrawal for the current and following year.

sources.title: Regulations of the PRC on Foreign Exchange Administration (State Council Decree No. 532)
sources.publisher: State Council of the PRC (published by SAFE Beijing)
sources.quote: 第五条　国家对经常性国际支付和转移不予限制。 / 第三十九条　有违反规定将境内外汇转移境外，或者以欺骗手段将境内资本转移境外等逃汇行为的……处逃汇金额30%以下的罚款；情节严重的，处逃汇金额30%以上等值以下的罚款
sources.supports: Current-account international payments and transfers are not restricted (Art. 5). FX-evasion/illegal-arbitrage penalties are up to 30% of the amount, or 30% to 100% in serious cases (Arts. 39, 40, 45); illegally carrying FX in/out is up to 20% (Art. 42).

sources.title: Interim Measures on Carrying Foreign Currency Cash In and Out of the Border (Huifa [2003] No. 102)
sources.publisher: SAFE and General Administration of Customs, published in the State Council Gazette
sources.quote: 携带不超过等值5000美元(含5000美元)的外币现钞出境的，无须申领《携带证》……原则上不得携带超过等值10000美元的外币现钞出境
sources.supports: Carrying foreign cash out: up to USD 5,000 needs no permit; USD 5,000-10,000 needs a bank-issued carrying permit; above USD 10,000 is in principle not allowed except in listed special cases with a SAFE permit.

sources.title: Administrative Rules on Individual's Foreign Exchange (PBOC Decree [2006] No. 3)
sources.quote: Article 7 Commercial banks and individuals shall abide by the Rules ... and must not evade limit administration by splitting large amount into small batches or tamper with authenticity administration by using fabricated commercial bills or vouchers. / Article 13 A non-domestic individual can convert legitimate renminbi income obtained in China under the current account into foreign exchange and remit abroad at a bank by showing valid identity documents and relevant documents.
sources.supports: Splitting a large amount into small batches to evade limits and fabricating documents are prohibited (Art. 7); non-domestic individuals may convert lawful current-account RMB income with ID and documents (Art. 13); an annual limit applies to FX sale/purchase (Art. 9).

sources.title: PBC official on the adjustment in the limit for cross-border transportation of national currency
sources.quote: the limit has a good reason to be reset at 20000 Yuan per person per time
sources.supports: The RMB 20,000 per person per trip cross-border cash limit. This is a PBC explanatory Q&A (2004) rather than the text of Announcement [2004] No. 18 itself, so the instrument number is carried from prior sessions and flagged.

sources.title: Provisional Administrative Rules on Sales and Payment of Foreign Exchange for Personal Asset Outbound Transfer
sources.quote: Emigrant asset transfer refers to encashment, exchange (at the commercial bank) and transfer overseas of assets by emigrants from Mainland China which they have obtained before they get immigration permission ... The first remittance may not exceed half of the total value of the assets applied to be transferred; less than half of the remaining value may be remitted one year after the first remittance; and the rest may be remitted outbound two years after the first remittance.
sources.supports: Emigrant and inheritor asset transfers are capital-account routes limited to those categories, approved by SAFE, and staged over up to two years for amounts at or above RMB 200,000; approvals at or above RMB 500,000 go to SAFE head office.

sources.title: Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (7th amendment)
sources.quote: For comprehensive income ... progressive tax rates ranging from 3 percent to 45 percent shall apply ... For income from business operation ... from 5 percent to 35 percent ... For income from interest, dividends or bonuses, income from leasing of assets, income from transfer of assets, and incidental income, a flat tax rate of 20 percent shall apply.
sources.supports: PRC IIT rates by income category; Article 1 defines resident individuals by domicile or 183 days' residence.

sources.title: Notice on Further Preventing and Handling Risks Related to Virtual Currency and RWA Tokenization (Yinfa [2026] No. 42)
sources.quote: 虚拟货币相关业务活动属于非法金融活动。在境内开展法定货币与虚拟货币兑换业务、虚拟货币之间的兑换业务……一律严格禁止，坚决依法取缔。
sources.supports: Converting between fiat currency and virtual currency inside mainland China is an illegal financial activity; the notice repeals Yinfa [2021] No. 237.

sources.title: Tariff of Accounts and Services for Wealth and Personal Banking Business (effective 31 October 2026)
sources.quote: 2.2.4.1 Telegraphic Transfer Issuance: Private Banking — For individual customer: Free; Premier — 0.1% of remittance amount Min. CNY100 / equivalent per transaction Max. CNY500 / equivalent per transaction Plus Cable Charge; Advance — same as Premier. 2.2.4.2 Cable Charges: Premier CNY120 / equivalent per cable; Advance CNY120; Private Banking individual Free. 2.2.6.1 Global Transfer to self-name HSBC accounts: Private Banking Free; Premier Free; Advance CNY145 (indicative; actual charge USD20).
sources.supports: The only published per-wire fee schedule used in this dashboard. It is a bank tariff for its own customer segments, not a regulator's rule, and it excludes other institutions' charges and taxes (Important Note 7).

sources.title: Yearly average currency exchange rates
sources.quote: The Internal Revenue Service has no official exchange rate. Generally, it accepts any posted exchange rate that is used consistently. ... China | Yuan | 7.129 (2025)
sources.supports: The 7.129 CNY/USD 2025 yearly average used for the USD restatement, and the fact that the IRS has no official rate (a consistent posted spot rate is generally accepted).

sources.title: 26 U.S.C. § 988 — Treatment of certain foreign currency transactions (2024 edition)
sources.quote: no gain shall be recognized ... by reason of changes in exchange rates after such currency was acquired by such individual and before such disposition. The preceding sentence shall not apply if the gain which would otherwise be recognized on the transaction exceeds $200.
sources.supports: Personal-transaction FX gain of USD 200 or less is not recognized under § 988(e)(2). The 2024 Code edition is the current GPO compilation available; later amendments are not reflected here (flagged).

sources.title: 31 CFR 1010.821 — Penalty adjustment and table
sources.quote: 31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(5)(B)(i) Foreign Financial Agency Transaction—Non-Willful Violation of Transaction ... Maximum ... $16,536; 31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(5)(C)(i)(I) ... Willful ... $165,353 (penalties assessed on or after January 17, 2025)
sources.supports: Inflation-adjusted FBAR civil penalty maximums assessed on or after 2025-01-17. The eCFR states its content is authoritative but unofficial; the annually published CFR/GPO edition is the official print.

sources.title: Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
sources.quote: the aggregate value of those foreign financial accounts exceeded $10,000 at any time during the calendar year reported
sources.supports: FBAR filing threshold and that whether the account produced taxable income is irrelevant to FBAR status.

sources.title: Comparison of Form 8938 and FBAR requirements
sources.quote: Specified individuals living outside the US: Unmarried individual (or married filing separately): more than $200,000 on the last day of the tax year, or more than $300,000 at any time during the year. Married individual filing jointly: more than $400,000 ... or more than $600,000 at any time.
sources.supports: Form 8938 thresholds for taxpayers living outside the US, alongside the FBAR USD 10,000 threshold.

sources.title: Instructions for Form 2555, Foreign Earned Income (tax year 2026)
sources.quote: For 2026, the maximum exclusion amount has increased to $132,900.
sources.supports: The 2026 foreign earned income exclusion amount, from the form instructions rather than the (stale) FEIE web page.

sources.title: Foreign earned income exclusion (web page cited by earlier sessions)
sources.doc_date: retrieved live; page text still shows 2020-2023 amounts
sources.supports: Evidence that the FEIE web page has not been updated past 2023; it must not be used for the 2026 amount, which is verified from VS19.

sources.title: Wise Help Centre — Guide to CNY transfers
sources.quote: Due to regulations, you can only send CNY from China to another account you own ... the maximum you can send in one transfer is 300,000 CNY ... a valid tax record issued by the China tax authority showing taxes paid within the last 3 years ... Set up a transfer and add a recipient to see the exact fees
sources.supports: Wise from-CNY eligibility, the CNY 300,000 per-transfer bank-app cap, the 3-year tax-record condition, and that fees are quoted only in-app.

sources.title: Send money from China
sources.quote: Passport (Excludes Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan passports) ... In China, a bank account may be required by the bank for sending money in cash. ... Pay the transfer fee.
sources.supports: Western Union IDs accepted, bank-account requirement may apply, and that no fee schedule or limit is published on the page.

sources.title: Money and Other Monetary Instruments (FinCEN Form 105)
sources.quote: Federal law mandates that when entering or leaving the United States you must report amounts exceeding $10,000 to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP).
sources.supports: A FinCEN Form 105 report is required for more than USD 10,000 of currency or monetary instruments carried into or out of the United States; failure risks seizure and civil or criminal penalties.

sources.title: Foreign Tax Credit
sources.quote: If you paid or accrued foreign taxes to a foreign country ... and are subject to U.S. tax on the same income, you may be able to take either a credit or an itemized deduction ... A foreign tax credit may not be claimed for taxes on income that you exclude from U.S. gross income
sources.supports: The US foreign tax credit is available only against US tax on the same income and cannot be claimed for taxes on excluded income.

method_notes.M01: Core route. Published HSBC fee applies to Premier/Advance individuals; for Private Banking individual customers items 2.2.4.1 and 2.2.4.2 are published Free. The tariff excludes other banks' charges and taxes.
method_notes.M02: Only available to domestic individuals, or foreign individuals holding a PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card (VS04). Not the general route for a US citizen without that card.
method_notes.M03: Published fee is Free for Private Banking and Premier; Advance is CNY 145 indicative (actual USD 20). CNY conversion still needs a lawful basis.
method_notes.M04: Own-account only. CNY 300,000 per transfer via the China bank app; fees only visible in-app, so blank here.
method_notes.M05: No published fee or limit; partner banks may require an account; passport accepted subject to bank rules.
method_notes.M06: RMB 100,000 per person per calendar year is a hard ceiling, so large balances cannot move this way quickly. Card-issuer fees vary and are not published here.
method_notes.M07: Published HSBC counter withdrawal fee is Free, but the cash FX spread, travel cost and insurer/transport risk are not published. USD 5,000 per trip without a permit is a hard ceiling for planning.
method_notes.M08: Offshore conversion cost and rate are outside the reviewed sources; the CNY 20,000 per trip ceiling (VS09, 2004) is the binding constraint. Verify current customs practice.
method_notes.M09: Only for RMB previously exchanged from foreign currency, with the original memo inside 24 months (VS03) and capped at the original exchange amount, which is not known.
method_notes.M10: Only for people who emigrated from mainland China with assets obtained before immigration permission; staged over up to two years for amounts at or above RMB 200,000 (VS10).
method_notes.M11: Inheritor transfer for foreign citizens inheriting mainland assets; SAFE approval and documentation; no published fee schedule.
method_notes.M12: Requires a lawful property sale and settled taxes; 20% IIT on the gain plus transaction taxes may apply; bank fees unpublished.
method_notes.M13: For registered individual foreign-trade operators with genuine trade flows; not available for a plain savings balance.
method_notes.M14: Rejected. Fiat-to-virtual-currency conversion in mainland China is an illegal financial activity (VS12); FX-violation penalties and uncapped losses may also apply.
method_notes.M15: Rejected. Splitting amounts to evade limits is expressly prohibited (VS08 Art. 7); FX penalties apply.
method_notes.M16: Rejected. Illegal FX trading (Art. 45) carries confiscation plus fines of up to 30%, or 30%-100% in serious cases.
method_notes.M17: Rejected. Fabricated documents to pass authenticity review fall under Arts. 40 and 48; criminal liability possible.
